question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ employees is drawn from a population. The population has employees with two different working hours, $38\,\text{h/week}$ and $40\,\text{h/week},$ distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than  $0.5\,\text{h/week}.$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the employees in the population have working hours $38\,\text{h/week}$ and $40\,\text{h/week},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $3+1=4$ employees only with the following working hours:

$$
38\,\text{h/week},\,38\,\text{h/week},\,38\,\text{h/week},\,40\,\text{h/week}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3\cdot 38+40) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(114+40) \\  & =\frac{154}{4} \\  & =38.5\,\text{h/week},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3\cdot {38}^{2}+{40}^{2})-{38.5}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(5\,932)-1\,482.25 \\  & =1\,483-1\,482.25 \\  & =0.75\,{(\text{h/week})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.75},$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5\,\text{h/week}.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{\sqrt{0.75}}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{{0.5}^{2}}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{0.25}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{3} \\ n & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=4.$
